findings.title: sqrtPriceX96 squared overflows uint256 before reaching FullMath.mulDiv

analysis.assetRisk: No asset risk -- overflow condition is unreachable
analysis.attackPath: Invalid -- requires price deviation of ~2^64x from stablecoin parity
analysis.conditions: sqrtPriceX96 > 2^128 requires one stablecoin to be worth ~18.4 quintillion of the other; exceeds total global economic value
analysis.impact: DoS of claim() -- but only at physically impossible price levels

findings.disagreementReason: The overflow requires approximately 18.4 quintillion x price deviation from stablecoin parity. This is not 'unlikely' but physically impossible given finite pool liquidity. Medium severity requires actual protocol impact, not mathematical edge cases in unreachable input regions. Any Uniswap pool with finite liquidity would be fully drained long before this price could be reached.
findings.submissionRecommendation: Include in QA report as code quality note. Not Medium.

findings.title: Hardcoded sUSDS_USDC_pool fallback creates unsettled deltas when reward token is not USDC

analysis.assetRisk: No asset loss -- PoolManager reverts safely on unsettled deltas
analysis.attackPath: Not an attack -- requires admin to change reward token AND forget to update pool
analysis.conditions: Two-step admin configuration where owner forgets second step; explicitly documented in code comments at lines 366-370
analysis.impact: DoS of execute() until admin updates pool configuration

findings.disagreementReason: Prior audit v04-M-03 adjudicated the identical pattern (admin forgets second config step after reward token change) and downgraded it to QA. The reasoning -- 'two-step owner configuration where owner forgets second step = admin mistake category' -- applies directly. Submitting this as Medium after the precedent downgrade would be inconsistent.
findings.submissionRecommendation: Include in QA report if desired. Not Medium per established precedent.

findings.title: claim() distributes yield tokens to claimer before collecting payment (CEI violation)

analysis.assetRisk: No asset risk -- nonReentrant modifier prevents exploitation
analysis.attackPath: Invalid -- reentrancy blocked; state pre-calculated; external strategy OOS per known issue #7
analysis.conditions: Would require: (1) yield strategy with callback, (2) bypassing nonReentrant, (3) manipulating pre-calculated state -- none achievable
analysis.impact: No demonstrated impact; economic scanner confirmed unexploitable

mitigationsPresent: nonReentrant modifier on claim() at line 566
Payment amount calculated from pre-read state before any transfers
External yield strategy behavior explicitly OOS per known issue #7
findings.disagreementReason: A CEI violation that is fully mitigated by nonReentrant and pre-calculated state is a code quality finding. C4 Medium requires actual protocol impact or value leak, not theoretical risk in a reentrancy-guarded function. The finding's own economic scanner confirmed it is 'not practically exploitable.'
findings.submissionRecommendation: Include in QA report as best-practice recommendation. Not Medium.
